tier_reason: Well-known independent suite (the-benchmarker/web-frameworks, 7.1k stars) runs fulmine.js and actix in one run with public code (javascript/fulmine.js/app.mjs, javascript/fulmine.js/config.yaml, javascript/config.yaml, rust/actix, rust/Dockerfile). Not A: there is no real CPU model, because the cpu_name is a hardcoded string in .tasks/db.rake.

corrections.claimed_speedup: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks data.json of 2026-09-24 (develop branch, commit f673364): fulmine.js 5.21 223,508 / 210,337 / 203,996 req/s at concurrency 64 / 256 / 512 vs actix (actix-web 4.8) 179,203 / 168,270 / 163,415 req/s, i.e. 1.25x at every level (derived from page data). The earlier snapshot on master (commit 0fccb1d, 2026-09-20, older method) shows 126,063 / 106,586 / 105,030 vs 115,638 / 102,329 / 99,835 req/s, i.e. 1.09x / 1.04x / 1.05x (derived from page data).
corrections.workload: the-benchmarker/web-frameworks develop-branch run of 2026-09-24 (commit f673364): zrk --closed, a closed loop over keep-alive connections (not oha with keep-alive disabled; the README method table dates that model to before 2026-08), 15 s per concurrency level 64/256/512. Each headline req/s is avg() over the three routes in .env (GET /, GET /user/0, POST /user) per .tasks/db.rake; the 1/3 fractions in the values fit a 3-route average. All handlers are hello-world (empty body or echoed id). fulmine.js runs with cluster:'auto' (one uWS worker per usable core, SO_REUSEPORT).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Node.js 26 (node 26-slim per javascript/config.yaml), fulmine.js ~5.21.0 on uWebSockets.js v20.71.0 (native C++ addon), NODE_ENV=production, EXPERIMENTAL_FASTCALL=1. actix-web 4.8 baseline: Rust 1.98 (rust:1.98-slim), cargo build --release with lto=true, codegen-units=1, panic=abort (rust/Dockerfile).
corrections.hardware: Undisclosed x86_64 Linux host (Fedora 44 kernel 7.2.6-200.fc44), 16 logical CPUs. The cpu_name 'M1 Eight-Core Processor' in data.json is a string hardcoded in .tasks/db.rake, not a measured CPU model. The framework container is pinned to cores 0-3 (SERVER_CPUS) and the load generator to cores 4-15 (LOAD_CPUS).
corrections.caveats: Low-star project (18 stars). fulmine.js is an Express-5-compatible layer over uWebSockets.js, whose C++ core does the HTTP work; the plain uwebsockets entry in the same run scores 174,621 req/s at c=512. The benchmark app turns on fulmine-specific options: 'declarative request values' lets the /user/:id route be answered by uWS in C++ without entering JavaScript, and etag and connection headers are off. Single synthetic hello-world workload. The suite changed load generator and model in 2026, and its README says results from different revisions are not comparable. The earlier snapshot still on master (commit 0fccb1d, 2026-09-20) gives different ratios, see claimed_speedup. There the lead over actix is only 4-9%. The suite's saturation probe reports identical values (0.995/0.992/0.988) for every framework checked, so it may not be a per-framework measure. Hardware metadata is inconsistent ('M1 Eight-Core Processor' on x86_64).

notes: The record's numbers match data.json on the default develop branch (commit f673364), not the master URL cited, so benchmark_url is pinned to that commit. The load model is corrected from oha without keep-alive to zrk --closed over keep-alive. Metadata verified: Apache-2.0, 18 stars, last commit 2026-09-23, not a fork, not archived.
